title: Circle
review: They exclusively chose Californians who love to talk, and so I was mostly on board with the evil scheme. It's hard to imagine the same thing with stoic Finnish people, or with Italians talking over each other. There are so many more fun stereotypes I can think of. It's a neat idea to cold open in a high-stakes balloon debate, but it's executed in a sloppy and visually dull way. It makes me think about how engaging {Locke} was visually, despite taking place entirely in a plain car, or how good the writing was in {It Ends} was, despite only being a conversation between four cosmically bored people. You can extend a single gimmick like this into a feature length plot and end up with something great, but the dialogue has to be razor sharp. It's not quite there in this film, but it did enough to win me over in time. It really helped that the cadence seemed to slow down, or at least each character gained more time to speak between votes.
spoilers: A little too much time was dedicated towards white people getting picked off one by one when they had right wing meltdowns. Those deaths were really predictable, when a character suddenly flips and decides to burn all their bridges. There could have been a bit more variety in that sense.
